To improve our development and focus on where it is needed. We use cookies for technical purposes and, with your consent, we will collect mainly Plugin version, Coordinator, Firmware version and Size of the network (number of router and number of end devices).

network.mesh.scans.subtitle: Stored scans of the Zigbee mesh, newest first. Pick one to draw it.
network.mesh.scans.empty: No scan stored yet. Launch a topology scan, then refresh this list: a scan takes several minutes and only appears once it has finished.
network.mesh.deleted.all: Every stored scan has been deleted
network.mesh.coverage.warning: {{answered}} of {{requested}} nodes answered this scan — the graph below shows only the part of the mesh that answered.
network.mesh.coverage.timeout: {{count}} node(s) were asked and never answered. On a zigpy scan each of them also costs the scan around 40 seconds of retries, every time it runs.
network.mesh.coverage.timeout.tree: {{count}} node(s) were asked for their associated devices and never answered.
network.mesh.coverage.notscanned: {{count}} node(s) have a neighbour table in principle, but this scan never reached them.
network.mesh.coverage.notscanned.tree: {{count}} node(s) were never asked for their associated devices.
network.mesh.noroutes: The {{source}} backend that wrote this scan collects no routing table, so the route overlay is unavailable here.
network.mesh.treeonly: This scan carries the associated devices only: it was collected on its own, without a topology scan, so there are no neighbour and no routing rows to draw. Launch a topology scan for the radio links.
network.mesh.graph.subtitle:
Zoom, pan and drag the graph. Click a node for its identity and its neighbour and routing rows, click a link for the LQI each end reported, click an arrow for the destinations it carries.
A node's icon says what the device is, its colour what part it plays in the mesh, and its border how it is doing.
network.mesh.graph.note: Each node is labelled with its name and its network id. A node with no name is labelled with its network id alone; the IEEE address is in the node panel.
network.mesh.hideisolated: Hide nodes with no visible link
network.mesh.counts.links.hidden: {{total}} links not drawn in this mode
network.mesh.counts.hops.hidden: {{total}} routing hops not drawn in this mode
network.mesh.counts.children.hidden: {{total}} association links not drawn in this mode
network.mesh.routesmode.note: Only routing hops are drawn, and they are all the same colour: a routing table row carries no LQI and no relationship. The LQI threshold and the relationship filters are greyed out because they have nothing to act on here.
network.mesh.treemode.note: Only the associated devices are drawn: for each router, the devices attached to it. It is the one view that places a battery device under its router, because the router answers for it. These links carry no LQI and no relationship, so the LQI window and the relationship filters are greyed out. The breadthfirst layout draws it best.
network.mesh.path.hint.none: No route is worked out until a device is picked. Pick the coordinator for how it reaches every device, or any other device for its route out.
network.mesh.path.hint.coordinator: How the coordinator reaches each device. Pick a device for its own route out.
network.mesh.path.hint.node: How this device reaches the coordinator.
network.mesh.path.summary.coordinator: {{routes}} route(s): {{estimated}} of them rest entirely on the LQI estimate, {{hops}} hop(s) estimated in all.
network.mesh.path.from.here.title: Show how this device reaches the coordinator
network.mesh.path.outcome.loop: The tables point in a circle
network.mesh.path.summary: {{hops}} hop(s): {{observed}} read from the tables, {{estimated}} estimated from the LQI.
network.mesh.path.none.unreachable: Nothing in this scan connects these two devices. Either a node on the way never answered, or there is genuinely no path.
network.mesh.path.none.loop: The routing rows lead back to a node already on the path. That is a snapshot taken while the routes were being rebuilt, not a loop the mesh is stuck in.
network.mesh.path.none.same: Source and destination are the same device.
network.mesh.path.manytoone: This mesh uses many-to-one routing towards the coordinator. Those routes live in route records held by the concentrator, which a topology scan cannot read, so the path shown here is the estimate.
network.mesh.path.caveat: This route is computed, not observed. It is worked out from one scan: the routing rows as they stood when the tables were read, and an LQI estimate wherever those rows ran out. A frame sent now may well take another path — routes are rediscovered when they fail, a device that has since woken, moved or been switched off changes the picture, and each radio applies its own link cost. Read it as the most likely path, and the dashed hops as this page's guess rather than the radios'.
network.mesh.orphans: {{count}} report row(s) name a node this scan does not list, and were not drawn.
network.mesh.contested: {{count}} device(s) are claimed by more than one router. That is a device that has reparented, leaving a stale entry behind in the table of the router it was on before; both links are drawn in red.
network.mesh.node.zdeviceid.unnamed: · reported, but not a device id this page has a name or an icon for.
network.mesh.node.zdeviceid.unknown: This device reported none, so it is drawn as a plain shape rather than as an icon.
network.mesh.node.parent.none: No router declares this device as attached to it.
network.mesh.node.parent.contested: More than one router claims this device: it has reparented, and the older entry is stale.
network.mesh.node.children.ambiguous: — on a scan that also reads neighbour tables, a router that was asked and timed out reads the same way.
network.mesh.node.note: Health, model, LQI, RSSI and battery are this device's values now, not its values at the time of the scan. The LQI here is the one the coordinator recorded for the device; a link's LQI is on the link.
network.mesh.node.neighbours.note: An LQI belongs to the node that reported it, so the two directions of one link usually differ. Depth is unreliable: a radio with no depth for a row answers with a sentinel value, which is reported here as unknown.
network.mesh.link.onesided: Only one of the two nodes reported this link. That can mean the other did not answer the scan, or that it does not hear this one.
network.mesh.link.note: A Zigbee neighbour table reports LQI only, so a link has no RSSI. Each node measures the link itself, which is why the two readings differ.
network.mesh.hop.subtitle: {{reporter}} reaches {{count}} destination(s) through {{nextHop}}.
network.mesh.hop.note: A routing table row says which neighbour a frame is handed to next, not the whole path. Follow the arrows from the source to see the hops a frame goes through.
network.mesh.value.scan_status.timeout.h: This node was asked and never answered. That is a gap in the picture, not a leaf without neighbours.
network.mesh.value.scan_status.not_suppo: An end device has no neighbour table to ask for. Expected, not a finding.
network.mesh.value.scan_status.not_scann: This node has a neighbour table in principle, but this scan never reached it.

tools.reporting.configure.title: Configure the reporting mechanism
tools.reporting.configure.subtitle:
Configure a device to automatically report the values of one or more of its attributes, or to receive such reports.
The minimum reporting interval field is 16 bits in length and SHALL contain the minimum interval, in seconds, between issuing reports of the specified attribute.
The maximum reporting interval field is 16 bits in length and SHALL contain the maximum interval, in seconds, between issuing reports of the specified attribute.
The reportable change field SHALL contain the minimum change to the attribute that will result in a report being issued. This field is of variable length.
For attributes with 'analog' data type (see 2.6.2), the field has the same data type as the attribute. The sign (if any) of the reportable change field is ignored.
tools.binding.title: Device Binds
tools.binding.subtitle:
Allow to bind a cluster between source and target devices
e.g. If you want to bind a Temperature sensor with an Actuator, the SourceIEEE/Ep will be the Temperature sensor, the DestIEEE/Ep will be the actuator and the Cluster will be 0402 (Temperature Measurement)

admin.firmware.nofirmware: No firmware file in the OTAFirmware folders
admin.firmware.device.unknown: version unknown until the device asks
admin.firmware.state.Waiting: Waiting for the device to ask
admin.firmware.state.Stalled: Stalled, resumes when the device asks
admin.firmware.confirm.title: Update the firmware
admin.firmware.cancel.title: Cancel the firmware update
admin.firmware.cancel.transfer: The device stops the download at once and keeps its current firmware.
admin.firmware.cancel.again: It is not updated again automatically (autoServeOTA) until the plugin restarts or you pick it again here.
